shape.name: Shape L — Pronunciation Noticing (Noticing-First)
shape.description: Noticing-first pronunciation lesson for plural -s (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/) in the context of personal possessions. Learners are first made to HEAR the gap between the L1-transfer version and the target (auditory discrimination), then the feature is isolated, linked to meaning, drilled, and used freely. An authentic recording from a past student serves as the final noticing text.
shape.pedagogical_justification: Pronunciation instruction that works is intelligibility-based (Levis, 2005; Munro & Derwing, 1995) and noticing-first (Schmidt, 1990): learners must consciously notice a feature in input for it to become intake. For Thai learners, plural -s is a critical case: final /s/, /z/ and /ɪz/ are often dropped or underarticulated, hiding the singular/plural distinction. Perception precedes production (final-consonant-deletion intervention literature), so the shape delivers auditory discrimination before drills.
shape.main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to notice and produce plural -s (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/) when talking about the things they own.

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to notice and produce plural -s (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/) in the context of talking about the things they own.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
31 August, 2026
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B1
Lesson Shape:
L (Pronunciation Noticing)
Materials:
Worksheet
Assessment:
Discrimination accuracy (Parts A-C), production observation during drills and the game (Part F)
Systems:
Pronunciation

stages.stage_aim: To activate the topic and elicit the target feature in natural speech
procedure: Show the splash slide. Ask: What do you see? What might this lesson be about? Let students speculate.
Advance to the title slide. Confirm the theme: the sounds at the end of plural words.
Ask: What things do you have on your desk, in your bag, at home? Elicit 3-4 answers. Write them on the board exactly as students say them, without comment.
Tell students the focus is the sounds at the END of plural words.

stages.stage_aim: To make the gap between L1 transfer and the target audible
procedure: Display the model sentence: I have three books, two dogs, and four glasses. Every plural -s sits before a pause or a vowel (salience-designed).
Play the comparison track: a narrator labels Thai English, then Standard English, readings of the model sentence.
Ask: Can you hear the difference? What disappeared?
Students tap the table on every plural /s/, /z/, /ɪz/ they hear in the Standard English version (Worksheet, Part A).
Feedback: the model sentence has three plural sounds: books, dogs, glasses.

stages.stage_aim: To perceive the target feature before producing it
procedure: Worksheet, Part B. Play the track: a narrator announces each number, a second voice says each word twice.
Students write ✓ if both repetitions carry the plural, or ✗ if the plural is dropped.
Check answers against the audited key (verified by listening, never guessed). Pattern: ✗ ✗ ✗ ✗ ✗.
Repeat any pairs students could not perceive. Note who still cannot hear the difference.

stages.stage_aim: To isolate the /s/, /z/, /ɪz/ endings and link them to meaning
procedure: Worksheet, Part C. Play the track: each word read once. Students write ✓ if they hear the plural ending, or ✗ if it is missing.
Worksheet, Part D. Students clap the syllables. Books = 1, dogs = 1, glasses = 2; reveal one count per click.
Elicit the rule: after voiceless sounds, -s sounds like /s/ (books); after voiced sounds, /z/ (dogs); after sibilants, /ɪz/ and adds a syllable (glasses).
Worksheet, Part E: circle the correct form — book is one, books is many.
Finger-tap drill on the model sentence: I have three books (1) and two dogs (2) and four glasses (3).
Backchain: glasses, four glasses, and four glasses, two dogs and four glasses, I have three books.
Choral and individual drill. Whisper-release drill: books, dogs, glasses — the final consonant must be heard.
Correct errors immediately. /ɪz/ words keep their extra syllable.

stages.stage_aim: To transfer the feature into spontaneous speech
procedure: Worksheet, Part F. Show the game slide and start the timer.
Pairs: A tells B two things they own. B holds up one finger for every plural /s/, /z/, /ɪz/ heard — one point per sound.
Dropped plural = do-over until B hears it. Swap after half the time.
Content feedback first, then language feedback on the most frequent dropped finals.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate noticing on authentic student speech and set up recycling
procedure: Worksheet, Part G. Play a past student's recording (Florence). Students tick or cross the numbered underlined plural targets.
The transcript is corrected ONLY in the target feature; all other grammar stays verbatim. [0] is the example item.
Reveal the audited key (verified by a teacher listening to the recording).
Worksheet, Part H. Play the model reading. Pairs read the paragraph to each other and tick or cross.
Quick-fire exit: books, dogs, glasses. Say them with the ending. Tell students the finals return in the next warm-up.

metadata.main_aim: By the end of the lesson, students will be better able to notice and produce plural -s (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/) when talking about the things they own.
metadata.subsidiary_aim: To notice that dropping the -s ending hides the singular/plural meaning.
answer_key: Part A: 3 plural sounds — books (/s/), dogs (/z/), glasses (/ɪz/).
Part B: 1. books/book — ✗ · 2. dogs/dog — ✗ · 3. glasses/glass — ✗ · 4. friends/friend — ✗ · 5. years/year — ✗. Pattern ✗✗✗✗✗ — all dropped.
Part C: answers require teacher audition — listen to the discrimination track and verify each tick/cross.
Part D syllables: books = 1, dogs = 1, glasses = 2, friends = 1.
Part E: 1. books · 2. dogs · 3. yes — glasses has 2 syllables, glass has 1.
Game: 1 point per heard plural /s/, /z/, or /ɪz/; do-over until the sound is heard.

Part G (Florence's transcript): ✓ = pronounced correctly, ✗ = plural dropped. Answers require teacher audition — the key must be verified by a teacher listening to the recording. 7 targets: [0] years (example, not scored) · [1] hours · [2] things · [3] friends · [4] books · [5] pictures · [6] books · [7] plants.

Part H (Model reading): 11 targets: [1] things (/z/) · [2] books (/s/) · [3] dogs (/z/) · [4] glasses (/ɪz/) · [5] friends (/z/) · [6] games (/z/) · [7] siblings (/z/) · [8] things (/z/) · [9] plants (/z/) · [10] pictures (/z/) · [11] things (/z/).
